items.longBusinessSummary: Applied Digital Corporation designs, develops, and operates digital infrastructure solutions to high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence industries in North America. It operates through: Data Center Hosting, and HPC Hosting Business. The company provides energized infrastructure services to crypto mining customers; and cloud services to customers, such as AI and machine learning developers. It also engages in the designing, constructing, and operating of data centers to provide computing power and support HPC applications. The company was formerly known as Applied Blockchain, Inc. and changed its name to Applied Digital Corporation in November 2022. Applied Digital Corporation is based in Dallas, Texas.

Title: The IREN Story Is Changing Fast. We See 82% Upside Potential
Author: Vandita Jadeja   Fri, September 25, 2026 at 8:30 PM GMT+2 5 min read
Published: 2026-09-25T18:30:34+00:00
=== BODY ===
IREN has shed its Bitcoin miner identity, with AI Cloud revenue doubling to $71M and a $2.4B Blue Owl financing deal sealing the pivot.
IREN's $4B contracted ARR, backed by Microsoft and NVIDIA deals, gives it a cleaner balance sheet than CoreWeave at half the market cap.
Even the bear case lands at roughly $67, above today's price, though a beta of 4 and -148% operating margin demand caution.
My 24/7 Wall St. price target for IREN (NASDAQ:IREN) is $84.29, implying 82.63% upside from the current price of $46.15. My recommendation is buy with a moderate 50% confidence level, reflecting both the scale of the AI Cloud opportunity and the very real execution risk of scaling GPU capacity across four continents.
IREN has stopped being a Bitcoin miner in any meaningful sense, and the market is still catching up to what that means.
IREN has climbed 8.28% over the past week and 22.19% year to date.
The catalyst was FY2026 results on August 27, 2026: revenue of $137.2 million missed estimates by 2.52%, with a GAAP net loss of $684 million driven almost entirely by a $450.4 million impairment on decommissioned Bitcoin mining hardware.
AI Cloud revenue more than doubled sequentially to $70.5 million. Days later, Blue Owl-managed funds led a $2.4 billion AI factory financing for IREN.
Many successful investors eventually reach the same moment. The saving is done, the portfolio is built, and the question quietly changes from how much can I grow this to how much can I take out? Get that second question wrong and decades of good investing can come apart in a handful of years.
The bull case rests on contracted revenue already signed. IREN has $4 billion of ARR contracted for 2026 capacity, of which $1 billion was operating as of late August. The $9.7 billion Microsoft deal and $3.4 billion, five-year NVIDIA AI Cloud contract plus up to $2.1 billion NVIDIA investment validate the platform.
Three-year contracts run above $20 million per megawatt of IT load, with discussions near $25 million per MW. Compass Point lifted its target to $105 after the Microsoft announcement.
If IREN delivers Horizons 2 through 4 on schedule and lands 2027 capacity at rising prices, my bull case points to roughly $86.60 within twelve months.
The bear case is execution. IREN carries a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.87, an operating margin of -148%, and FY2027 capex guidance of $25 billion to $30 billion. Customer concentration in Microsoft and NVIDIA is real, and Reddit sentiment has swung, with a very bearish reading around a thread titled "Why IREN is a hard pass for me" in early September.
The counterfactual matters: those losses are largely non-cash, operating cash flow was $1.81 billion in Q4, and adjusted EBITDA margin ran at 41% in Q2 FY26. My bear case scenario still lands at roughly $66.81, above today's price.
CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) is the direct pure-play AI cloud comparison. CRWV carries a market cap near $40 billion on a $104 billion backlog and 1.5 GW of active power. CRWV's debt-to-equity of 8.94 dwarfs IREN's 1.87, making IREN the cleaner balance sheet at half the market cap.
Applied Digital (NASDAQ:APLD) is the closest data-center pivot comparison, with a $7.66 billion market cap and its first 100 MW direct-to-chip liquid-cooled facility operational. APLD posted Q3 revenue of $126.6 million, similar to IREN's Q4. IREN's larger contracted ARR and NVIDIA relationship justify a valuation premium.
Cipher Mining (NASDAQ:CIFR) is the fellow ex-Bitcoin miner with 700 MW of contracted HPC capacity and $11.4 billion in contracted revenue. CIFR trades at a $7.5 billion market cap. IREN's larger 2026 ARR ramp and NVIDIA-backed contract make my $84.29 target reasonable.
My 24/7 Wall St. price target of $84.29 and buy rating rest on contracted, funded ARR ramping into revenue over the next four quarters.
The setup rewards investors who believe IREN can bring Horizons 2 through 4 online in the December quarter without slippage. IREN sits alongside the power, cooling, and networking names we profiled in a free report on seven AI infrastructure stocks that aren't chipmakers. Caution is warranted if GPU financing markets tighten or hyperscaler capex plans slow. On balance, the setup favors owners.

Title: Cipher Digital Jumps 4% as Barber Lake Lease Extension Lifts Contracted Revenue Past $9B; TeraWulf and Applied Digital Gain 2%
Author: David Moadel   Fri, September 25, 2026 at 3:16 PM GMT+2 4 min read
Published: 2026-09-25T13:16:05+00:00
=== BODY ===
Cipher Digital's Barber Lake extension covers a 300 MW Texas site for 20 years, generating up to $9B in revenue with Google backing Fluidstack's obligations.
UBS initiated Buy ratings on five AI data-center companies, estimating the group holds 5 gigawatts leased and 12 gigawatts of expansion potential.
Construction timelines, ERCOT grid connections, and financing requirements still determine when long-term contracts convert into actual operating revenue.
The AI infrastructure trade is moving higher as investors focus on long-term power access and contracted revenue, with Cipher Digital leading a group that includes TeraWulf and Applied Digital. The latest move comes as Cipher Digital's Barber Lake agreement provides a longer revenue runway, while recent Wall Street coverage has also highlighted the potential for former Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) miners to convert power assets into AI data-center infrastructure.
Cipher Digital (NASDAQ:CIFR) stock is up 4% to $18.74 as the company's Barber Lake lease extension puts more attention on its contracted AI infrastructure revenue. The agreement with Fluidstack covers the full 300-megawatt Barber Lake site in Texas, with the lease structure extending to as much as 20 years and roughly $9 billion of potential revenue if the available extensions are exercised.
The Barber Lake arrangement gives Cipher Digital a larger contracted revenue base while reinforcing the company's shift away from Bitcoin mining and toward high-performance computing infrastructure. Google also provides financial support for Fluidstack's obligations, adding another layer of credit backing to the project.
Cipher Digital has also been working through the power-access question that has become central to AI data-center development in Texas. ERCOT has issued conditional grid-capacity designations for several Cipher Digital projects, although those designations don't represent final approval for active hookups, leaving construction, interconnection and delivery timelines as important factors.
Recent coverage from UBS Group (NYSE:UBS) adds another layer to the sector's momentum, with UBS initiating coverage on five AI data-center companies and assigning Buy ratings across the group. UBS cited constrained compute supply and access to power as important advantages for companies transitioning from cryptocurrency mining into AI infrastructure.
The UBS coverage includes TeraWulf and Applied Digital alongside Cipher Digital, with the bank estimating that the five companies collectively have roughly 5 gigawatts of leased capacity and another 12 gigawatts of potential expansion. UBS also expects AI infrastructure requirements to grow substantially through the end of the decade, although the companies still face construction, financing and execution risks.
TeraWulf (NASDAQ:WULF) stock is up 2% to $16.55, while Applied Digital (NASDAQ:APLD) stock is also up 2% to $27.51. Both companies are part of the broader group of former or current digital-asset infrastructure operators seeking to monetize large power positions through AI and high-performance computing customers.
TeraWulf has signed major AI infrastructure agreements, including a long-term arrangement with Anthropic, while Applied Digital has continued developing large-scale data-center capacity for AI workloads. The market response to Cipher Digital's latest news therefore extends beyond one company, as investors consider whether long-term contracts can make power-rich infrastructure assets more valuable.
The broader Global X Data Center & Digital Infrastructure ETF (NASDAQ:DTCR) is up 4% to $29, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 0.49% to $744.70. That gap suggests the data-center infrastructure group is attracting stronger buying interest than the broader technology-heavy index during this session.
A key issue for Cipher Digital, TeraWulf and Applied Digital remains the difference between contracted capacity and operational capacity. Long-term leases can provide substantial revenue visibility, but construction schedules, grid connections, financing requirements and customer delivery milestones still determine when those contracts translate into actual operating revenue.
For Cipher Digital, the Barber Lake extension could give the market another reason to focus on the company's contracted revenue rather than its legacy mining operations. Investors may want to watch for signs that ERCOT designations progress toward usable power capacity and that Cipher Digital continues meeting its construction milestones, while keeping position sizes modest given the execution risks.

Title: Applied Digital vs. IREN: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Author: Sara Appino, The Motley Fool   Thu, September 24, 2026 at 8:22 PM GMT+2 5 min read
Published: 2026-09-24T18:22:20+00:00
=== BODY ===
As the race for artificial intelligence infrastructure intensifies, investors are looking for the next big winner. Should you bet on Applied Digital (NASDAQ:APLD) or IREN (NASDAQ:IREN) for your portfolio?
Both companies are evolving from legacy crypto roots into powerhouse providers of high-performance computing and data center services. While they share a similar mission of powering the AI revolution, their contract structures and growth trajectories differ significantly. This comparison breaks down their financials and business models to help you decide which stock fits your strategy.
In its latest annual report, Applied Digital highlighted its design and operation of digital infrastructure for AI and cloud workloads, positioning it among tech stocks focused on North American data centers. The company primarily focuses on its AI Factory campuses, where the flagship Polaris Forge 1 site is fully contracted to CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV). Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as a single entity drives a huge portion of revenue.
In FY 2026, revenue reached nearly $611.3 million, representing growth of roughly 183.7% compared to the previous year. This massive surge was driven by the expansion of its high-performance computing segments. The company reported a net loss of close to $244.0 million, resulting in a negative net margin of approximately 39.9%, a metric that shows what percentage of revenue remains as profit after all expenses.
As of its May 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is 4.0x, indicating the company has four dollars in current assets for every one dollar in short-term liabilities. The debt-to-equity ratio, which compares total debt to shareholder equity, is roughly 2.9x. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 245.5% of operating cash flow, meaning reported cash generation is heavily inflated by this non-cash add-back.
According to its latest annual report, IREN is building next-generation data centers and AI cloud infrastructure while transitioning from legacy Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) mining. It recently secured a five-year, nearly $9.7 billion contract with Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) for data center capacity. Additionally, IREN signed a five-year cloud services agreement worth roughly $3.4 billion with Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) to support its ongoing expansion.
In FY 2026, revenue reached close to $707.0 million, which is an increase of roughly 41.1% over the prior year. The company reported a net loss of nearly $702.6 million, leading to a negative net margin of approximately 99.4%. This reflects the complex nature of transitioning between two energy-heavy business models and managing the associated growth costs.
According to its June 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 3.6x, which suggests it has sufficient short-term assets to cover its immediate obligations. The debt-to-equity ratio is close to 1.9x, showing the company uses nearly two dollars of debt for every dollar of equity. Free cash flow for the year was roughly negative $2.2 billion as the company scales its future infrastructure offerings.
Applied Digital faces significant customer concentration, making it highly dependent on a small number of partners. It requires intensive capital and relies on frequent debt or equity financing to fund its projects. Most operations are concentrated in North Dakota, exposing the business to localized infrastructure risks and potential asset obsolescence from rapid technological shifts.
IREN struggles with financial instability, evidenced by its significant net loss in FY 2026. The transition from legacy Bitcoin mining to AI Cloud Services carries operational strain and potential regulatory scrutiny regarding energy usage. High leverage with nearly $7.98 billion in total debt and reliance on hardware suppliers like NVIDIA, Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL), and Supermicro add further layers of risk.
Applied Digital offers a lower P/S ratio based on sales over the past twelve months.
I'd go with IREN, though Applied Digital is doing interesting things in its own right. Applied Digital beat revenue estimates in its most recent quarter, a contract with CoreWeave provides long-term revenue visibility, and the company is building AI data center capacity at a rapid pace. For investors comfortable with early-stage risk, it is worth watching.
But IREN's transformation from Bitcoin miner to AI cloud infrastructure company is one of the more striking pivots in the market right now. It reported $4 billion in contracted annual recurring revenue for its 2026 capacity and has Microsoft as a customer. Nvidia has officially certified IREN as a reference-quality cloud provider for its most advanced chips, essentially giving it a stamp of approval that the company knows how to operate AI infrastructure at the highest level.
Both companies are losing money and spending heavily to build out infrastructure, so this is not a space for the faint of heart. But for a patient investor willing to sit through the volatility, IREN's contracted revenue base and blue chip customer relationships are a more solid foundation to build on over time.
